notes: The RTL contains no additional entities in the supplied file, so both FIFO instances are treated as black-box instances of another IP.
The received and transmitted data concepts pass through FIFO and serial forwarding paths without a separate conceptual holding register, consistent with their Phase 1 descriptions.

points.reason: A bus write directly overwrites ctrl.enable, allowing unauthorized disabling or interruption of the UART.
This point only forwards the stored enable value and the RTL shows no independent read, write, or blocking mechanism there.
A bus write changes the stored prescaler and baud fields, allowing timing corruption or a transfer stall.
This logic only derives a clock value from the stored prescaler; no independent unauthorized access is shown at this point.
The receiver reloads its timing counter from the configured baud value as designed, with no separate access mechanism at this block.
The transmitter reloads its timing counter from the configured baud value as designed, with no separate access mechanism at this block.
The serial input is sampled and shifted into the received byte, so changing uart_rxd_i changes the reconstructed data.
The internal receive byte is present on rx_fifo.wdata and can be observed or changed before FIFO storage.
The write-enable controls whether a completed received byte is accepted by the receive FIFO, so suppressing it can lose data.

points.reached by: bus_access --> rx_fifo.clear via ctrl.clr_rx, ctrl.enable, and ctrl.sim_mode
points.reason: The clear control can erase or disable the receive FIFO path and thereby discard received bytes.

points.reached by: bus_req_i --> rx_fifo.re via bus_req_i.addr, bus_req_i.rw, and bus_req_i.stb
points.reason: A bus read drives the FIFO read request and releases received data toward the response; suppressing the request can prevent servicing.
Under the black-box rule, the FIFO stores incoming received bytes, returns them on rdata_o, and can be cleared, written, or read through its mapped controls.
The bus access returns FIFO data in bus_rsp_o.data and also accepts writes that clear or disable the receive path.
Bus write data enters the transmit FIFO and a disable or clear control can discard queued transmit bytes.
The transmitted byte is visible and controllable on the FIFO write-data path.

points.reached by: bus_req_i --> tx_fifo.we via bus_req_i.addr, bus_req_i.rw, and bus_req_i.stb
points.reason: The write-enable decides whether a bus-provided transmit byte enters the FIFO, so suppressing it can prevent transmission.

points.reached by: bus_access --> tx_fifo.clear via ctrl.clr_tx, ctrl.enable, and ctrl.sim_mode
points.reason: The clear logic can erase queued transmit data or disable the transmit FIFO path.
Under the black-box rule, the FIFO buffers transmit bytes, returns them on rdata_o, and can be cleared, written, or read through its mapped controls.
The transmitter loads and shifts the queued byte toward the serial output, while CTS and transmitter state can hold or block progress.
The serial output directly exposes each transmitted data bit.
The synchronized CTS input affects the transmit state transition and can hold the transmitter in a waiting state.
The control process computes uart_rtsn_o from enable, hardware flow control, and receive FIFO occupancy; its result can assert backpressure or permit reception.
The process generates irq_rx_o from receive FIFO status and programmable interrupt enables, so the indication can be suppressed or asserted incorrectly.
The process generates irq_tx_o from transmit FIFO status and programmable interrupt enables, so the indication can be suppressed or asserted incorrectly.
